topics.topic: Whether KeyFieldsContent must require unique ports or define canonical handling for duplicate-port fields
questions: KeyFieldsContent permits multiple fields entries with the same port, but preserving one object member per entry would repeat that member name and canonical_bytes must reject it; must fields be constrained to unique ports, or must duplicate-port handling replace one of these requirements?

judgement.why: This asks the same duplicate-port canonicalization question as P1, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: How duplicate ports in fields entries must be handled during canonicalization
quotes: content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For the idempotency_key variant MUST build one JSON object with one member per entry of fields, named by the entry's port and holding the JSON value its canonical_json encodes, so the order of the fields does not change the key, and return the hexadecimal SHA-256 of its canonical bytes; a field whose value is null is kept as null, not dropped.

canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1), which an IEEE double cannot hold exactly, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.
KeyFieldsContent fields (exact, no others exist): subject_kind: Literal['idempotency_key'], fields: tuple[JsonPayload, ...]
JsonPayload fields (exact, no others exist): payload_kind: Literal['json'], port: str, canonical_json: bytes
precedent.why: The texts require a member for every entry but neither prohibit duplicate ports nor define how multiple entries with the same object-member name are reconciled.

topics.topic: Handling symbolic links during run spool removal
questions: When remove_run_spool encounters a symbolic link inside the run spool, must it raise StoreInternalError without removing anything, or unlink the symbolic link as part of removing everything?

quotes: Every file and directory under the data directory MUST be opened without following symbolic links; a symbolic link met by any call after start makes that call raise StoreInternalError with nothing written.

MUST remove the spool directory of run_id and everything in it without following symbolic links, and return normally when the spool is already absent or the run is unknown; it never removes anything outside that one run's spool and writes no record.
judgement.why: The general policy requires an error with nothing removed when a link is met, while the removal requirement says to remove everything without following links.

A supported value_schema is a JSON object using only type as one string among null, boolean, integer, number, string, array and object, enum as a non-empty array of distinct scalars, const as one scalar, properties and required for object, additionalProperties true or false only, items as one schema for array, minItems, maxItems, minLength, maxLength, minimum and maximum, nested schemas following the same rule; any other keyword is outside the subset; a file port's value_schema is the empty object.
judgement.why: The schema requirement treats value_schema as a JSON object, including an empty object for files, while the Port contract requires a string.

Use only the IMPORTS listed above plus required standard library imports.

topics.topic: Handling kernel actors in non-read flow activation
questions: For a non-read activation requested with an Actor whose kind is 'kernel', must the function reject that actor, record under the given kernel actor, or obtain an owner actor not supplied by the contract?

quotes: activate_flow_version: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise UnknownReferenceError for an unknown flow version; then prove it again with prove_version and raise RefusedError carrying the proof failure when it is not proven; then raise RefusedError when the actor is an agent and highest_effect_class is above read, even when that version is already active, keeping nothing.

activate_flow_version: [BEHAVIOR] When the version already is its flow's latest activation it returns that FlowActivation and records nothing; otherwise it writes one ActivateFlowVersionChange through record_change with the proven highest_effect_class and activated_at from kernel_now, under the kernel actor when that class is read and under the given owner actor otherwise, which replaces the previous activation at once while started runs keep their pinned version.
ActorKind enum values: 'owner', 'agent', 'kernel'; Python member names were not available in models context.
judgement.divergence: One implementer rejects a kernel actor requesting a non-read activation because the required actor is an owner; another records the activation under the supplied kernel actor because only agents are expressly refused. The caller notices whether activation succeeds, and the owner or store consumer notices which actor is recorded.
judgement.why: The texts do not determine how a supplied kernel actor is handled when the proven effect class is above read.

topics.topic: Whether constants may satisfy fan-in by targeting flow outputs
questions: Can a constant satisfy fan-in for a flow output, or are constants forbidden from targeting flow outputs?

quotes: MUST run nine phases in this fixed order and return at the first failing check, items within a phase in that phase's order and conditions of one item in the order listed: 1 nodes by node_id, a function node names a contract version that read_contract_version finds and an operation node names a binding that read_binding finds with status accepted; 2 constants by to_node then to_port, the port exists and is an input port of a node, never a flow output, of value carriage, the constant's declared value_schema equals the port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema text for a one port, the canonical array schema with it as items for a many port) — composition already refused a value that does not fit its declared schema, so no separate value check runs here; 3 edges in edge order, both ports exist with the right direction, carry equal value_schema text, the same carriage and for files the same media type, a flow endpoint port being value carriage; 4 guards in edge order, the guard port is an output of one cardinality of the edge's source node, that node has no map_over, its schema is a closed set with enum or const, and the guard value is a member.
judgement.why: Phase 2 expressly requires every constant to target a node input and never a flow output.

topics.topic: Behavior when find_send_authority returns None
questions: Must reach_operation_element always call send_under_authority after find_send_authority, or must it instead request approval and return without calling it when the authority is None?
Must reach_operation_element always call send_under_authority after find_send_authority, or must it skip that call and request or reuse an approval when find_send_authority returns None?

quotes: then for a non-read binding asks find_send_authority with the prepared request_digest; then calls send_under_authority with the run, the element, the given inputs, the binding, the prepared request, the authority found (None for a read binding) and the actor.

When find_send_authority returns None MUST, unless an approval of the element with status requested already exists, write one RequestApprovalChange for the element with the binding_id, input_digests, the prepared request_digest and an ApprovalPreview of the operation's service_id, operation_name and effect_class, the prepared request description and the element's input PortRefs; input_digests are the digests of every input value and file in input port name order, list elements in list order. Nothing is sent and the element waits with reason owner_approval for that approval, the existing requested one when there was one, even if its request_digest differs.

authority is None exactly for a read binding: reach_operation_element passes a non-read binding only with the Authority find_send_authority found, and otherwise requests an approval instead of sending; a non-read binding given authority None, or a non-read SendResult whose attempt_status is None, is a broken invariant raised as StoreInternalError, nothing sent or written for the former.
judgement.why: The orchestration note requires the send call after authority lookup, while the other passages require a non-read operation with no authority to request approval without sending.

topics.topic: EffectAttempt handling when spool_file is refused for a read binding
questions: For a read binding whose spool_file call is refused, must there be no EffectAttempt, or must an attempt remain applied?

quotes: For a read binding no EffectAttempt is written, no authority is recorded, and the attempt number used for spooling is the count of the element's NodeExecutions read with ExecutionsOfElement plus one.
a RefusedError from spool_file turns the outcome into contract_violation with no outputs, the attempt still applied.
judgement.why: One passage forbids an EffectAttempt for every read binding, while the spool-refusal passage says the attempt remains applied without excluding read bindings.

topics.topic: Whether FileListPayload supports multiple files with distinct list_index values
questions: Must each content of a FileListPayload be spooled with a distinct list_index, or are many-file outputs forbidden?

quotes: FileListPayload fields (exact, no others exist): payload_kind: Literal['file_list'], port: str, contents: tuple[bytes, ...]
Cardinality enum values: 'one', 'many'; Python member names were not available in models context.

otherwise each JSON output is published with put_value_bytes and becomes a StoredValue of value carriage with the output port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items), its size and the class the binding declares for that port, and a file output is published with spool_file under SpooledFileKey of the run, node, map_index, this attempt_number, the port and no list_index, becoming a SpooledFile of the port's declared class, which every port of a binding has, since a proposal leaving out a port's class is refused (A08 rule 5, M01), so that class is always a DisclosureClass member; a RefusedError from spool_file turns the outcome into contract_violation with no outputs, the attempt still applied.

outputs, only when that outcome is succeeded, one StoredValuesRef or SpooledFilesRef per output port in port name order, a SpooledFilesRef with the class the binding declares for that port, and no outputs otherwise; and no resources_used.
judgement.divergence: One implementer rejects a many-file FileListPayload as a contract violation because every spool key is required to have no list_index; another accepts it and publishes its contents as multiple files, so the caller observes failure versus success and a different output file set.
judgement.why: The texts define many-file payloads and many-cardinality ports but specify only a no-list_index spooling rule, without saying whether such outputs are unsupported or how their individual files are keyed.

topics.topic: How failed-attempt spool cleanup must be supported or whether its no-retention requirement should be removed
questions: Which passage must change: should a per-attempt/per-file spool-removal operation be imported, should spool_file provide atomic all-or-nothing publication, or should the requirement that no file of the failed attempt is kept be removed? a RefusedError from spool_file concluding resource_exhausted with the SandboxResult's resources_used, no outputs and no file of that attempt kept.
judgement.why: The required attempt-local file cleanup cannot be performed by the only imported removal operation, which removes the entire run spool.

topics.topic: Whether cleanup_failed in a mapped function element permits later execution or requires an immediate stop
questions: For a mapped function element that crashes with detail cleanup_failed, must later elements still execute because a failed element does not stop them, or must execution stop immediately and raise StopRequiredError?

quotes: a waiting or failed element does not stop the elements after it, and a concluded element is never executed again.

When a function element's outcome is crashed with detail cleanup_failed MUST write that one execution in a RecordRunProgressChange with status running and the waiting points unchanged, execute and reach nothing more, write no other status, and raise StopRequiredError.
judgement.why: One passage requires later mapped elements to continue after a failed element, while the cleanup_failed rule requires execution to stop immediately.

topics.topic: Whether initialize, ping, and tools/list are exempt from naming a catalogue operation
questions: Must every JSON-RPC request name a catalogue operation as the first passage requires, or must initialize, ping, and tools/list be accepted without naming one as the second passage requires?
Must every JSON-RPC request name and invoke a catalogue operation, or are initialize, ping and tools/list handled without satisfying that requirement?

quotes: MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record; the message names a catalogue operation and fits that operation's request model with no unknown field — a field typed X | None fitting when it is absent or JSON null — and every bound below, else invalid_request; the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else not_permitted; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1).

A request's method decides: initialize answers the result {protocolVersion: the imported MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant, capabilities: {tools: {listChanged: false}}, serverInfo: {name: the imported MCP_SERVER_NAME constant, version: the imported MCP_SERVER_VERSION constant}} whatever version its params ask, and keeps no state; ping answers an empty result object; tools/list answers {tools: [...]} as below, ignoring any cursor; tools/call names the catalogue operation in params.name and carries its request in params.arguments, which then pass the remaining checks of the first note.
judgement.divergence: One implementation rejects initialize, ping, and tools/list because they do not name catalogue operations; another accepts and handles those protocol methods directly, which MCP callers notice in their initialization, health-check, and tool-discovery responses.
judgement.why: The universal ordered-check rule requires the message to name a catalogue operation, while the method-specific rule requires three non-catalogue protocol methods to be answered directly.

precedent.topic: Whether notifications and responses are subject to body-size and token refusal checks
quotes: MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record;
The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.

A JSON object whose jsonrpc is "2.0" with a string method and an id is a request; one with a method and no id is a notification and one with no method a response: both are answered with empty bytes and change nothing.
precedent.why: Size and token checks occur before the body is read and classified, so an oversized or unauthenticated notification or response is refused before the empty-response rule can apply.

precedent.topic: Precedence among HTTP Origin, path, and method rejections
quotes: Only a POST to the path equal to the imported MCP_ENDPOINT_PATH constant reaches answer_request; any other method on that path is answered 405, any other path 404, and a request carrying an Origin header 403, each without a body and without calling answer_request;
precedent.why: The Origin condition is unconditional, while 405 is limited to the correct path and every other path receives 404.

precedent.topic: Whether refusal bodies stay unread or are parsed to preserve the JSON-RPC id
quotes: The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.
The id of every response is the body's id member when the body is one JSON object whose id is a string or an integer, and null otherwise; reading it checks nothing and decides nothing.
precedent.why: The body is not read before size and token checks, so refusals at those checks cannot recover its id and use null.
